q-107835.name: Question 1
q-107835.problem:
Which of the following integrals are equivalent to $Γ(z)$ for $\text{Re}(z)>0?$

I. $2{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{{e}^{-{t}^{2}}}{{t}^{2z-2}}\,\text{d}t$

II. $2{\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{{t}^{z}}{{e}^{{t}^{2}}}\,\text{d}t$

III. $2{\int }_{0}^{\infty }{t}^{2z-1}{e}^{-{t}^{2}}\,\text{d}t$
q-107835.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the definition of the gamma function:

$$
Γ(z)={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{t}^{z-1}{e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t,\,\text{Re}(z)>0.
$$

With this definition in mind, let's consider each of the given integrals.

- Integral I does *not* match the definition. The integrand $\frac{{e}^{-{t}^{2}}}{{t}^{2z-2}}$ is not equivalent to that shown in the definition.

- Integral II does *not* match the definition. The lower bound of integration does not match that given in the definition.

- Integral III matches the definition. We use a substitution $s={t}^{2},$ then $2t\,\text{d}t=\text{d}s.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}2{\int }_{0}^{\infty }{t}^{2z-1}{e}^{-{t}^{2}}\,\text{d}t & =2{\int }_{0}^{\infty }{t}^{2(z-1)+1}{e}^{-{t}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{t}^{2(z-1)}{e}^{-{t}^{2}}(2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{s}^{z-1}{e}^{-s}\,\text{d}s=Γ(z).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

$$

$$
Γ(\frac{1}{2})+Γ(\frac{3}{2})=\sqrt{\pi }+\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\pi }=\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{\pi }.
$$

q-107883.name: Question 14
q-107883.worked_solution:
To evaluate the gamma function at multiples of one-half, we use the following recursive formula:

$$
Γ(z+1)=zΓ(z),\,Γ(\frac{1}{2})=\sqrt{\pi }
$$

So, we have the following:

$$
Γ(\frac{3}{2})=\frac{1}{2}Γ(\frac{1}{2})=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\pi },
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}Γ(\frac{7}{2}) & =\frac{5}{2}\,Γ(\frac{5}{2}) \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{3}{2}\,Γ(\frac{3}{2}) \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\pi } \\  & =\frac{15}{8}\sqrt{\pi }\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{4}{\sqrt{\pi }}\,Γ(\frac{7}{2})+\frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi }}\,Γ(\frac{3}{2})=\frac{4}{\sqrt{\pi }}\cdot \frac{15}{8}\sqrt{\pi }+\frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi }}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\pi }=8.
$$

$$
Γ(z+1)=zΓ(z),\,Γ(\frac{1}{2})=\sqrt{\pi }

$$
\begin{aligned}Γ(\frac{7}{2})=\frac{5}{2}Γ(\frac{5}{2})=\frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{3}{4}\sqrt{\pi }=\frac{15}{8}\sqrt{\pi }\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\frac{8}{3}\sqrt{\pi }\,Γ(\frac{7}{2})+\frac{4}{3}\sqrt{\pi }\,Γ(\frac{5}{2})=\frac{8}{3}\sqrt{\pi }\cdot \frac{15}{8}\sqrt{\pi }+\frac{4}{3}\sqrt{\pi }\cdot \frac{3}{4}\sqrt{\pi }=6\pi .
$$
